title: Credit Committee Basis Note: Measuring a Member's Whole Crop Input Position
content:
Credit on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts is measured across the member's whole input position rather than account by account.

**The measure.** Combined exposure is what is owed on every input account of the member that is not closed, less the prepay held to their credit on those same accounts, and it is measured against the sum of the limits those accounts carry.

**The release condition.** Product is released against an account only where the combined exposure after the invoice would stay at or under the combined limit, so a member sitting at their ceiling on one account cannot be supplied by writing the ticket on the other. The account the ticket is written on must itself be live — an account that is active, or active and flagged past due — and the test is made before the product is released, against the cooperative's own record of the account: its programme, its limit, the balance standing on it and its reference number.

**The grain allowance.** A member who also holds a live grain marketing contract for the current crop year on a programme the grain catalogue marks patronage-eligible carries a working allowance above their combined limit equal to the delivered value of the bushels still owed on those contracts, because that grain is coming to the cooperative and will settle here. That allowance falls away the moment the contract is cancelled, defaulted or fully settled, and it is never counted twice against two accounts.

**Where the exposure would be passed.** The desk releases what fits inside the ceiling, holds the balance and refers the member to credit; it never releases product over the ceiling and asks credit afterwards.

## Worked reading (hypothetical figures)

A member holds two open accounts of the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts. Owed on the two together: 168000 USD. Prepay held to their credit on them: 20000 USD. Combined exposure is therefore 148000 USD. The limits the two accounts carry come to 175000 USD. A ticket of 30000 USD would take the exposure to 178000 USD, above the combined limit, and the part that fits inside the ceiling is 27000 USD: that much is released, the balance is held, and the member is referred to credit.

Had the same member held a live grain marketing contract for the current crop year on a patronage-eligible programme with bushels still owed to a delivered value of 40000 USD, the working allowance would carry the ceiling to 215000 USD for as long as those bushels stand owed, and the whole ticket would be released.
